sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿憂深虛遠，殊沃朕心，始終倚賴，未可執辭也。」

translations.literal: The edict said, "Your concern is deep, broad, and far-reaching, and it especially enriches my heart. I have relied on you from beginning to end, and you may not insist on resigning."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Your concern is deep, broad, and far-reaching, and it especially enriches my heart. I have relied on you from beginning to end, and you may not insist on resigning."

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，詔還朝，攝冢宰，充山陵使，賜號「尚父」，進位太尉、中書令，增實封通計二千戶，給一千五百人糧，二百匹馬草料，所領諸使副元帥並罷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong ascended, an edict recalled him to court; he served as acting chief minister, was made tomb commissioner, was granted the title "Sublime Father," promoted to Grand Commander and Grand Counselor of the Central Secretariat, with total actual enfeoffment increased to two thousand households, provision for fifteen hundred men's rations, fodder for two hundred horses; all his various deputy commander commissions were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, an edict recalled Ziyi to court. He served as acting chief minister and tomb commissioner, was granted the title "Sublime Father", promoted to Grand Commander and Chief Minister of the Secretariat, with total actual enfeoffment raised to two thousand households, rations for fifteen hundred men, and fodder for two hundred horses. All his deputy commander posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 諸子弟女婿拜官者十餘人。

translations.literal: His sons, younger brothers, and sons-in-law who received official appointments numbered more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten of his sons, younger brothers, and sons-in-law received official appointments.

sentences.zh: 建中二年夏，子儀病甚，德宗令舒王誼傳詔省問。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, in summer, Ziyi was gravely ill; Dezong ordered Prince of Shu Yi to convey an edict to inquire after his health at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong, in summer Ziyi fell gravely ill. Dezong sent Prince Shu Yi to convey an imperial edict inquiring after his health.

sentences.zh: 及門，郭氏子弟迎拜於外，王不答拜；

translations.literal: When he arrived at the gate, the Guo family's sons and younger brothers came out to welcome and bow; the Prince did not return the bow;
translations.idiomatic: At the gate, the Guo sons and younger brothers came out to welcome him and bow; the prince did not bow in return.

sentences.zh: 子儀臥不能興，以手叩頭謝恩而已。

translations.literal: Ziyi lay abed and could not rise; he merely knocked his head with his hand to thank the grace.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi lay abed and could not rise; he could only knock his head with his hand in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 六月十四日薨，時年八十五，德宗聞之震悼，廢朝五日，詔曰：天地以四時成物，元首以股肱作輔，公臺之任，鼎足相承，上以調三光，下以蒙五嶽。允釐庶績，鎮撫四夷，體元和之氣，根貞一之德，功至大而不伐，身處高而更安。尚父比呂望之名，為師增周公之位，盛業可久，歿而彌光。故太尉、兼中書令、上柱國、汾陽郡王、尚父子儀，天降人傑，生知王佐，訓師如子，料敵若神。昔天寶多難，羯胡作禍，咸秦失險，河洛為戎。公能扶翼肅宗，載造區夏。於國有患，勞其戡定；於邊有寇，藉其驅除。安社稷必在於絳侯，定羌戎無逾於充國。絳臺綏四散之眾，涇陽降十萬之虜。勛高今古，名璟夷狄，而勞乎征鎮，二紀於茲。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the sixth month he died, aged eighty-five. When Dezong heard of it, he was shaken and grieved and suspended court for five days. The edict said: Heaven and earth complete things through the four seasons, and the sovereign makes assistants through his arms and legs. The offices of the dukes and ministers support one another like the legs of a tripod; above, they regulate the three lights, and below, they cover the Five Marchmounts. Truly ordering the many achievements, pacifying the four barbarians, embodying the qi of primal harmony, and rooting oneself in the virtue of pure unity: his achievement was supremely great, yet he did not boast; his person occupied high place, yet was all the more secure. As Sublime Father, he matched the name of Lü Wang; as teacher, he increased the rank of the Duke of Zhou. His flourishing enterprise can endure long, and after death it shines still more. The late Grand Commandant, concurrently Director of the Secretariat, Pillar of State, Prince of Fenyang Commandery, and Sublime Father Ziyi was a human hero sent down by Heaven, born knowing how to assist a king. He trained troops as if they were his sons and judged the enemy as if by spirit. Formerly, when Tianbao had many troubles and the Jie barbarian created disaster, Xianyang and Qin lost their defenses and the Yellow River and Luo region became enemy ground. The Duke was able to support and assist Suzong and recreate the realm. When the state had distress, it labored him to settle it; when the frontier had invaders, it relied on him to drive them off. To secure the altars of state, one must look to Jiang Hou; to pacify the Qiang and Rong, none surpassed Chongguo. At Jiang Terrace he reassured scattered multitudes; at Jingyang he received the surrender of a hundred thousand captives. His merit is high in present and past, his name bright among the barbarians, yet he labored in campaigns and garrisons for twenty-four years.

sentences.zh: 頃以春秋既高，疆埸多事，罷彼旌鉞，寵在臺衡。

translations.literal: Recently, as his years were already advanced and the frontier had many affairs, those battle-axes were removed from him, and favor rested in the council chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Of late, as his years had grown great and the frontier was troubled, we took the command from his hands and honored him in the halls of state.

sentences.zh: 以公柱石四朝，籓翰萬里，忠貞懸於日月，寵遇冠於人臣，尊其元老，加以崇號，期壽考之永，養勛賢之德。

translations.literal: Because you, sir, were the pillar stone of four reigns, a frontier bulwark for ten thousand li, your loyalty and constancy hung like sun and moon, your favor and treatment crowned among ministers—we honored our elder statesman and added a lofty title, hoping for longevity everlasting, nurturing the virtue of meritorious worthies.
translations.idiomatic: You were the pillar of four reigns, a bulwark on the frontier for ten thousand li; your loyalty shone like sun and moon, your honors surpassed all ministers. We honored our elder statesman with a lofty title, hoping for long life, that the virtue of a great servant might be preserved.

sentences.zh: 膏肓生疾，藥石靡攻，人之云亡，梁木斯壞。

translations.literal: Sickness arose in the vitals beyond cure; medicines and stones could not prevail; the man is said to be gone—the ridgepole is now broken.
translations.idiomatic: Sickness took hold in the marrow of his bones; no medicine could save him. The man is gone—the ridgepole of the house is broken.

sentences.zh: 雖賻禮加等，輟朝增日，悼之流涕，曷可弭忘！

translations.literal: Though funeral gifts were raised in grade and court was suspended for added days, mourning with streaming tears—how can this be forgotten!
translations.idiomatic: Though we raise the funeral gifts and extend the days of mourning, our grief flows in tears that cannot be stilled.

sentences.zh: 更議追崇，名位斯極，而尊為尚父，官協太師，雖爵秩則同，而體望尤重。

translations.literal: Further deliberation on posthumous honors—his name and rank reach the utmost; and to honor him as Sublime Father, his office accorded as Grand Preceptor—though noble rank is the same, yet in substance and prestige he is especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: We deliberate further on posthumous honors, for his name and rank have reached their height. To honor him as Sublime Father and accord him the office of Grand Preceptor—though the noble rank is the same, the weight of esteem is greater still.

sentences.zh: 斂以袞冕，旌我元臣。

translations.literal: Let him be enshrouded in the robe and cap of rank, displaying our foremost minister.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be laid in the robes of highest rank, that we may honor our greatest minister.

sentences.zh: 聖祖園陵，所宜陪葬，式墓表文終之德，象山追去病之勛。

translations.literal: At the imperial ancestral tombs, he ought to be buried alongside, that the tomb may express the virtue of his life's end, like Mount Xiang commemorating Huo Qubing's merit.
translations.idiomatic: He should be buried beside the imperial tombs, that his grave may mark the virtue of his life's end, as Mount Xiang marked the merit of Huo Qubing.

sentences.zh: 千載如存，九原可作，冊命之禮，有司備焉。

translations.literal: For a thousand years as though still living, in the dark realm he may yet be raised—the rites of enfeoffment proclamation, let the relevant offices prepare them.
translations.idiomatic: For a thousand years he will seem still alive; in the dark realm he may yet be summoned forth. Let the relevant offices prepare the rites of enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 可贈太師，陪葬建陵。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and buried alongside at Jian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and granted burial beside the Jian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 仍令所司備禮冊命，賻絹三千匹、布三千端、米麥三千石。

translations.literal: Moreover, let the relevant offices prepare the rites and enfeoffment proclamation; funeral gifts of three thousand bolts of silk, three thousand pieces of cloth, and three thousand shi of rice and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Let the relevant offices further prepare the rites of enfeoffment. Funeral gifts: three thousand bolts of silk, three thousand lengths of cloth, and three thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 舊令一品墳高丈八，而詔特加十尺。

translations.literal: The old regulation set first-rank tombs at one zhang and eight chi in height, but the edict specially added ten chi.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation a first-rank tomb stood one zhang and eight chi high; the edict specially added ten chi more.

sentences.zh: 群臣以次赴宅吊哭。

translations.literal: The ministers in turn went to his residence to mourn and weep.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers went in turn to his house to mourn and weep.

sentences.zh: 兇喪所須，並令官給。

translations.literal: All needs for the funeral were ordered supplied by the government.
translations.idiomatic: All expenses of the funeral were to be supplied by the state.

sentences.zh: 及葬，上御安福門臨哭送之，百僚陪位隕泣，賜謚曰忠武，配饗代宗廟庭。

translations.literal: When he was buried, the Emperor went to Anfu Gate to mourn in person and see him off; the hundred officials took their places accompanying him, weeping as they fell; he was granted the posthumous title Zhongwu, and enshrined in sacrifice at Emperor Daizong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial, the Emperor went to Anfu Gate to mourn and see him off in person; the hundred officials stood in attendance, weeping as they fell. He was granted the posthumous name Loyal and Martial and given a place in sacrifice at Emperor Daizong's temple.

sentences.zh: 子曜、旰、晞、昢、晤、曖、曙、映等八人，婿七人，皆朝廷重官。

translations.literal: His sons Yao, Gan, Xi, Pan, Wu, Ai, Shu, Ying—eight in all—and seven sons-in-law were all important officials of the court.
translations.idiomatic: His eight sons—Yao, Gan, Xi, Pan, Wu, Ai, Shu, and Ying—and seven sons-in-law all held high office at court.

sentences.zh: 諸孫數十人，每群孫問安，不盡辨，頷之而已。

translations.literal: His grandsons numbered several tens; whenever a crowd of grandsons came to greet him, he could not distinguish them all and merely nodded.
translations.idiomatic: He had several dozen grandsons; when they came in groups to greet him, he could not tell them apart and merely nodded.

sentences.zh: 參佐官吏六十餘人，後位至將相，升朝秩貴位，勒其姓名於石，今在河中府。

translations.literal: Over sixty assistant officials, who later reached positions of general or chancellor, rose to noble ranks in court—their names were carved on stone; they are now at Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: More than sixty staff officers later rose to the rank of general or chancellor; their names were carved in stone, and the stele stands today in Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 人士榮之。

translations.literal: Scholars and officials took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Men of standing counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 史臣裴垍曰：汾陽事上誠藎，臨下寬厚，每降城下邑，所至之處，必得士心。

translations.literal: The historiographer Pei Ji said: Fenyang served his sovereign with sincere devotion, was generous and lenient toward those below; whenever he reduced a city or subordinate town, wherever he went he inevitably won the hearts of the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer Pei Ji wrote: The Duke of Fenyang served his sovereign with whole-hearted loyalty and treated those below with generous kindness. Wherever he took a city or town, he won the hearts of the gentry.

sentences.zh: 前後遭罹幸臣程元振、魚朝恩譖毀百端，時方握強兵，或方臨戎敵，詔命徵之，未嘗不即日應召，故讒謗不能行。

translations.literal: Before and after he suffered slander in countless ways from favored ministers Cheng Yuanzhen and Yu Chao'en; though at the time he held strong troops or was facing enemy hosts, whenever an edict summoned him he never failed to respond that very day—therefore slander could not take effect.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again the favored ministers Cheng Yuanzhen and Yu Chao'en slandered him by every means. Yet whether he then held a great army or stood face to face with the enemy, he never failed to answer an imperial summons that same day—so calumny could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 代宗幸陜時，令以數十騎覘賊，及在涇陽，又陷於胡虜重圍之中，皆以身許國，未嘗以危亡易慮，亦遇天幸，竟免患難。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong visited Shan, he ordered him with several dozen horsemen to reconnoiter the enemy; and when at Jingyang he again fell into heavy encirclement by the barbarian hosts—all times he pledged his body to the state, never changing his resolve because of peril or ruin; he also met heaven's fortune and ultimately escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong fled to Shan, Ziyi rode out with a few dozen men to scout the enemy; at Jingyang he fell again into heavy encirclement by the barbarians. Each time he offered his life to the state and never wavered for fear of death or ruin—and each time heaven favored him, and he escaped disaster.

sentences.zh: 田承嗣方跋扈魏州，傲狠無禮，子儀嘗遣使至，承嗣西望拜之，指其膝謂使者曰：「茲膝不屈於人若干歲矣，今為公拜。」

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi was then domineering at Weizhou, arrogant, fierce, and without decorum; Ziyi once sent an emissary there—Chengsi bowed toward the west and, pointing to his knees, told the envoy: 'These knees have not bent to anyone for how many years—today they bow for you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi then ruled Weizhou with brutal arrogance and would bow to no one. Once when Ziyi sent an envoy, Chengsi turned west and bowed, then pointed to his knees and said to the messenger: "These knees have not bent to any man in many years—today they bend for your lord."

sentences.zh: 李靈曜據汴州，公私財賦一皆遏絕，獨子儀封幣經其境，莫敢留之，必持兵衛送。

translations.literal: Li Lingyao held Bian Prefecture; public and private wealth and tax revenues were all intercepted and cut off—only when Ziyi's sealed tribute passed through his territory did no one dare detain it; they invariably escorted it with armed guard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingyao held Bian Prefecture and seized all public and private wealth and tribute that passed through—except Ziyi's sealed gifts. No one dared hold those back; armed escorts saw them safely through.

sentences.zh: 其為豺虎所服如此。

translations.literal: Such was how he was obeyed by wolves and tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the awe he commanded from wolves and tigers alike.

sentences.zh: 麾下老將若李懷光輩數十人，皆王侯重貴，子儀頤指進退，如僕隸焉。

translations.literal: Veteran generals under his command, such as Li Huai'guang and dozens like him—all were kings, marquises, and great nobles; Ziyi nodded and pointed for their advance and retreat, like household servants.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran commanders under his banner, such as Li Huai'guang and dozens besides—all princes and great nobles—obeyed Ziyi's nod and gesture to advance or retreat as though they were household servants.

sentences.zh: 幕府之盛，近代無比。

translations.literal: The splendor of his staff—none in recent times compared.
translations.idiomatic: No staff in recent memory matched his in grandeur.

sentences.zh: 始與李光弼齊名，雖威略不逮，而寬厚得人過之。

translations.literal: From the beginning he was equally famed with Li Guangbi; though in martial prestige and strategy he did not match him, in generous lenience and winning people he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: From the first he stood equal in fame with Li Guangbi; though he did not match Guangbi in martial prestige and strategy, he surpassed him in generous kindness and in winning men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 歲入官俸二十四萬貫，私利不在焉。

translations.literal: Annual official salary income was two hundred forty thousand strings of cash; private profit was not among it.
translations.idiomatic: His official salary came to two hundred forty thousand strings of cash a year; private gain was not counted among it.

sentences.zh: 其宅在親仁里，居其里四分之一，中通永巷，家人三千，相出入者不知其居。

translations.literal: His residence was in Qinren Ward, occupying a quarter of the ward; a long lane ran through the middle; household members numbered three thousand—those entering and leaving did not know where he lived.
translations.idiomatic: His mansion stood in Qinren Ward and filled a quarter of the ward; a long lane ran through its center. Three thousand household members came and went, and visitors could scarcely tell where the master lived.

sentences.zh: 前後賜良田美器，名園甲館，聲色珍玩，堆積羨溢，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Before and after he was granted fertile fields, fine vessels, famed gardens and superior halls, music, women, rare treasures—piled up overflowing, beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years he was granted fertile lands, fine vessels, famous gardens and splendid halls, music, courtesans, and rare treasures—heaped up beyond measure or count.

sentences.zh: 代宗不名，呼為大臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong did not call him by name; he called him 'Great Minister.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong never spoke his name; he called him only Great Minister.

sentences.zh: 天下以其身為安危者殆二十年。

translations.literal: The realm relied on his person for safety or peril for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years the realm's safety or ruin rested on his person alone.

sentences.zh: 校中書令考二十有四。

translations.literal: Twenty-four times he was assessed as zhongshuling.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four times he received the highest assessment as Chief Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 權傾天下而朝不忌，功蓋一代而主不疑，侈窮人欲而君子不之罪。

translations.literal: His power tilted the realm yet the court did not resent him; his merit covered a generation yet the sovereign did not doubt him; his extravagance exhausted human desire yet the gentleman did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: His power bent the realm yet the court did not envy him; his merit outshone a generation yet the throne did not doubt him; his luxury exceeded all ordinary desire yet upright men did not condemn him.

sentences.zh: 富貴壽考，繁衍安泰，哀榮終始，人道之盛，此無缺焉。

translations.literal: Wealth, nobility, long life, prolific offspring, peace and security, sorrow and glory from beginning to end—the fullness of the human way, in this none was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth, rank, long life, many sons, peace and safety, honor in life and glory in death—the full measure of human fortune, in him nothing was wanting.

sentences.zh: 唯以讒怒，誣奏判官戶部郎中張譚杖殺之，物議為薄。

translations.literal: Only because of slander and rage did he falsely memorialize and have his judicial officer, Household Bureau Director Zhang Tan, beaten to death—the public opinion deemed him petty.
translations.idiomatic: Only once, moved by slander and anger, did he falsely accuse and have his aide, Household Bureau Director Zhang Tan, beaten to death—an act for which public opinion judged him harshly.

sentences.zh: 子 曜曜，子儀長子。

translations.literal: Son: Yao—Yao was Ziyi's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yao. Yao was Ziyi's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 性孝友廉謹。

translations.literal: By nature filial, friendly, honest, and careful.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was filial, brotherly, honest, and restrained.

sentences.zh: 子儀薨，出征於外，留曜治家，少長千人，皆得其所。

translations.literal: When Ziyi died, he was on campaign abroad; he left Yao to manage the household; young and old, a thousand people—all found their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi died, Yao was away on campaign and had been left to manage the household. Young and old, more than a thousand in all, each found his proper place under his care.

sentences.zh: 諸弟爭飾池館，盛其車服，曜以儉樸自處。

translations.literal: His younger brothers vied to adorn pools and halls and to display their carriages and robes; Yao maintained himself in plain simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers competed to ornament their pools and halls and to parade fine carriages and robes; Yao kept to plain and simple ways.

sentences.zh: 累遷至太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was promoted cumulatively to Crown Prince's Guest.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in office to become Guest of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 建中初，子儀罷兵柄，乃遍加諸子官，以曜為太子少保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, when Ziyi was stripped of military power, he then broadly promoted all his sons in rank, appointing Yao as Crown Prince's Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianzhong era, after Ziyi was relieved of military command, he had all his sons promoted in rank and appointed Yao Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 子儀曜遵遺命，四朝所賜名馬珍玩，悉皆上獻，德宗復賜之，曜乃散諸昆弟。

translations.literal: Yao, following Ziyi's testamentary command, presented to the throne all the famous horses and precious curios bestowed by four reigns; Dezong returned them as gifts, and Yao then distributed them among his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Following Ziyi's dying wish, Yao surrendered to the throne every famous horse and precious object the four reigns had bestowed on the family. Dezong gave them back, and Yao divided them among his brothers.

sentences.zh: 子儀薨後，楊炎、盧杞相次秉政，奸諂用事，尤忌勛族。

translations.literal: After Ziyi died, Yang Yan and Lu Qi in succession held power; wicked flatterers ran affairs and especially resented clans of merit.
translations.idiomatic: After Ziyi's death, Yang Yan and Lu Qi held the reins of government in turn. Sycophants and schemers ran the court and bore special enmity toward families of martial merit.

sentences.zh: 子儀之婿太僕卿趙縱、少府少監李洞清、光祿卿王宰，皆以有人告訐細過，相次貶黜。

translations.literal: Ziyi's sons-in-law—Grand Master of Studs Zhao Zong, Assistant Supervisor of the Palace Workshop Li Dongqing, and Director of the Imperial Household Wang Zai—because people reported petty offenses against them, were one after another demoted and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi's sons-in-law—Grand Master of Studs Zhao Zong, Assistant Supervisor of the Palace Workshop Li Dongqing, and Director of the Imperial Household Wang Zai—were demoted one after another when informers denounced them for trifling faults.

sentences.zh: 曜家大恐，賴宰相張鎰力為庇護。

translations.literal: Yao's household was greatly alarmed; they relied on Chancellor Zhang Mi's strong protection.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao household was terrified, and owed its safety to Chancellor Zhang Mi's vigorous protection.

sentences.zh: 奸人幸其危懼，多論奪田宅奴婢，曜不敢訴。

translations.literal: Villains, rejoicing in their fear, seized many fields, houses, and slaves and bondmaids; Yao did not dare appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Predators, scenting their fear, stripped them of fields, houses, and servants; Yao did not dare protest.

sentences.zh: 德宗微知之，詔曰：「尚父子儀，有大勛力，保乂皇家，嘗誓以山河，琢之金石，十世之宥，其可忘也！其家前時與人為市，以子儀身歿，名被誣構，欲論奪之，有司無得為理。」詔下方已。

translations.literal: Dezong learned something of the matter and issued an edict: "Shangfu Ziyi had great merit and strength, preserving and protecting the imperial house. We once swore by mountains and rivers and carved it in metal and stone that his house would be pardoned for ten generations; can this be forgotten? Previously his household made a sale with another, and because Ziyi has died, his name has been falsely accused and they wish to litigate and seize it. The responsible offices may not hear the case." Only after the edict was issued did the harassment stop.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong learned something of the matter and issued an edict: "Shangfu Ziyi had great merit and strength, preserving and protecting the imperial house. We once swore by mountains and rivers and carved it in metal and stone that his house would be pardoned for ten generations; can this be forgotten? Previously his household made a sale with another, and because Ziyi has died, his name has been falsely accused and they wish to litigate and seize it. The responsible offices may not hear the case." Only after the edict was issued did the harassment stop.

sentences.zh: 曜居喪得禮，若儒家子，服未闋寢疾，或勸其茹蔥薤，曜竟不屬口。

translations.literal: Yao observed mourning with proper rites, like a Confucian scholar; before the mourning period ended he took to bed with illness; some urged him to eat scallions and leeks, but Yao would not let them pass his lips.
translations.idiomatic: Yao mourned with the punctilio of a scholar; before the mourning term was complete he fell bedridden. Some urged him to eat scallions and leeks, but he would not touch them.

sentences.zh: 建中四年三月卒，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: He died in the third month of Jianzhong year four and was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of Jianzhong year four and was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 晞，子儀第三子。

translations.literal: Xi was Ziyi's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was Ziyi's third son.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，常從父征伐。

translations.literal: From youth he was skilled at riding and archery and often followed his father on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he excelled at horsemanship and archery and often rode with his father to war.

sentences.zh: 初以戰功授左贊善大夫，從廣平王收復兩京，晞力戰於香積寺、陜西，皆出奇兵克捷，以功加銀青光祿大夫、鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Initially for battlefield merit he was made Left Advisor-in-Attendance; following the Prince of Guangping in recovering the two capitals, Xi fought hard at Xiangji Temple and west of Shaan, both times winning with surprise forces; for merit he was promoted Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Master of Ceremonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He first earned the post of Left Advisor-in-Attendance for battlefield merit. When he followed the Prince of Guangping in retaking the two capitals, Xi fought fiercely at Xiangji Temple and west of Shaan, winning both times with unexpected maneuvers. For these deeds he was made Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Master of Ceremonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 後河中軍亂，殺節度使李國貞、荔非元禮於絳，詔以子儀為河東關內副元帥，鎮絳州，時四方擾叛，多逐戎帥，子儀至絳，誅其元惡，其黨頗不自安，欲謀翻變。

translations.literal: Later the Hezhong army mutinied and killed Military Governors Li Guozhen and Lifei Yuanli at Jiang; an edict made Ziyi vice commander-in-chief of Hedong and Guannei, stationed at Jiang. At the time disturbances and rebellions were everywhere and many ousted their military commanders; when Ziyi reached Jiang he executed the ringleaders, and their followers were quite unsettled and plotted mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Hezhong army mutinied, killing Military Governors Li Guozhen and Lifei Yuanli at Jiang. Ziyi was ordered to serve as vice commander-in-chief of Hedong and Guannei and take station at Jiang. Rebellion roiled on every side and commanders were being driven out everywhere; when Ziyi arrived at Jiang he executed the ringleaders, and their followers grew restless and plotted a revolt.

sentences.zh: 晞知其謀，選親兵四千，伏甲以防之，常持弓警夜，不寐者凡七十日，叛將竟不敢發，以功拜殿中監。

translations.literal: Xi learned of the plot; he selected four thousand trusted troops, hid armor to guard against it, constantly held his bow on night watch, and did not sleep for seventy days in all; the rebel generals ultimately dared not act; for merit he was appointed Director of the Palace Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Xi learned of the plot. He picked four thousand trusted men, concealed armor to meet any outbreak, and kept bow in hand on the night watch—sleeping not at all for seventy days. The rebel generals never dared move. For this service he was made Director of the Palace Administration.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年，僕固懷恩誘吐蕃、回紇入寇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangde, Pugu Huai'en induced Tibet and the Uyghurs to invade.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 2 (763), Pugu Huai'en incited Tibet and the Uyghurs to raid the borders.

sentences.zh: 加晞御史中丞，領朔方軍以援邠州，與馬璘合勢，大破蕃軍。

translations.literal: Xi was made Assistant Censor-in-Chief and led the Shuofang army to relieve Bin Prefecture; joining forces with Ma Lin, he thoroughly defeated the Tibetan army.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was promoted to Assistant Censor-in-Chief and led the Shuofang army to relieve Bin Prefecture. Combined with Ma Lin's forces, he routed the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，懷恩誘虜再寇邠州，陣於涇北，子儀令晞率步卒五千、騎軍五百，出西南掩擊之。

translations.literal: That winter Huai'en induced the barbarians to invade Bin again; they formed battle lines north of Jing; Ziyi ordered Xi to lead five thousand foot soldiers and five hundred cavalry, sortie southwest and strike them from the flank.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Huai'en again lured the barbarians against Bin. They drew up north of Jing, and Ziyi ordered Xi to take five thousand infantry and five hundred cavalry and sweep in from the southwest.

sentences.zh: 晞以兵寡不敵，持而不戰，及至晡晚，乘其半濟而擊之，大破獯虜，斬首五千級。

translations.literal: Xi, with few troops unable to match them, held and did not give battle; when evening came he struck as they were half across the river and thoroughly defeated the Xiongnu barbarians, beheading five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, Xi held his ground and refused battle. At dusk, as the enemy were half across the river, he struck and shattered them, taking five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 是時連戰皆捷，詔加御史大夫，子儀固讓不受，

translations.literal: At this time victories came in succession; an edict added Censor-in-Chief, but Ziyi firmly declined and would not accept,
translations.idiomatic: Victories followed one after another. The throne offered Xi the post of Censor-in-Chief, but Ziyi steadfastly refused on his behalf,

sentences.zh: 永泰二年，檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In Yongtai year two, he was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai year two, he was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 大歷七年，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In Dali year seven, he was granted the honorific Opening an Office Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali year seven, he was granted the honorific Opening an Office Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 十二年，丁母憂；

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he entered mourning for his mother;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he went into mourning for his mother;

sentences.zh: 服除，加檢校工部尚書，判秘書省事，

translations.literal: when mourning ended he was made Acting Minister of Works and charged with overseeing the Palace Secretariat,
translations.idiomatic: when the mourning term ended he was made Acting Minister of Works with charge over the Palace Secretariat,

sentences.zh: 建中二年，丁父喪，持服京城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, entered mourning for his father, observing the full term in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong, then entered mourning for his father and kept the full term of grief in the capital.

sentences.zh: 朱泚構逆，遣人就第問訊，欲令掌兵，晞佯瘖，噤口不言，泚以兵脅之，晞終不語，賊知其不可用，乃止。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci plotted rebellion; he sent someone to Xi's residence to inquire and wished to put him in command of troops; Xi feigned muteness, sealed his lips and would not speak; Ci used troops to threaten him, but Xi never uttered a word; the rebels knew he could not be used and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci rose in rebellion and sent men to Xi's house to sound him out, hoping to put him at the head of troops. Xi played the mute and would not open his mouth. Ci threatened him with soldiers, yet Xi never spoke. The rebels saw he was useless and left him alone.

sentences.zh: 晞潛奔奉天，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Xi secretly fled to Fengtian and barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Xi stole away to Fengtian and barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 初，晞兄曜襲父代國公，實封二千戶，及曜卒，詔曰：「故尚父、太尉中書令、汾陽王，功格上玄，道光下土，積其善慶，垂裕無窮。雖嫡長雲殂，支宗斯盛，汾陽舊邑，盍有丕承。其男前左散騎常侍、駙馬都尉、食實封五百戶曖，夙稟義方，居忠履孝，儷崇銀榜，攄美金章，繼撫先封，允宜聽復。曖兄檢校工部尚書、守太子賓客、趙國公晞，並弟右金吾將軍、祁國公、食實封二百五十戶曙，太子左諭德映等，並休有令名，保其先業，宜允推恩之典，以明延嗣之誠。其實封二千戶，宜準式減半，餘可分襲。曖可襲代國公，仍通前襲三百戶；晞可二百五十戶；曙可五十戶，通前三百七十戶；映可二百三十五戶。」尋又詔尚父子儀男晞、曖、映、曙四人所襲實封，各減五十戶，以賜郭曜男鉾、郭晤男鐇，各襲一百戶。

translations.literal: At first, Xi's elder brother Yao inherited their father's title Duke of Dai with a fief of two thousand taxable households. When Yao died, an edict said, "The late Sublime Father, Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Fenyang had merit that reached high Heaven and a Way that shone upon the lower earth; he accumulated goodness and blessings and left endless abundance. Although the legitimate eldest line has now died, the collateral branches flourish. How could the old fief of Fenyang not have a great successor? His son Ai, former Left Regular Attendant, Commandant-Consort, and holder of a fief of five hundred taxable households, long received righteous instruction, dwelt in loyalty, and walked in filial piety; he matched the exalted silver tablet and displayed beauty in gold insignia. It is truly fitting to permit him to resume and continue the former fief. Ai's elder brother Xi, Acting Minister of Works, acting Guest of the Heir Apparent, and Duke of Zhao, together with his younger brothers Shu, General of the Right Golden Guard, Duke of Qi, and holder of a fief of two hundred fifty taxable households, and Ying, Left Adviser to the Heir Apparent, all have fine reputations and preserve their ancestor's enterprise. It is fitting to permit the canon of extending grace, to make clear the sincerity of continuing the line. The two thousand taxable households should be halved according to regulation, and the remainder may be divided for inheritance. Ai may inherit the Dukedom of Dai, with three hundred households in all together with the former inheritance; Xi may receive two hundred fifty households; Shu may receive fifty households, making three hundred seventy households together with the former grant; Ying may receive two hundred thirty-five households." Soon another edict reduced by fifty households each the fiefs inherited by the Sublime Father Ziyi's sons Xi, Ai, Ying, and Shu, and gave them to Yao's son Mou and Guo Wu's son Fan, each inheriting one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 晞至行在，復檢校工部尚書、太子詹事；

translations.literal: When Xi reached the emperor's camp he was again made Acting Minister of Works and Tutor of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: When Xi reached the imperial camp he was again made Acting Minister of Works and Tutor of the Heir Apparent;

sentences.zh: 從駕還京，改太子賓客。

translations.literal: following the emperor back to the capital, he was changed to Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: after escorting the emperor back to the capital, he was reassigned as Companion of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 晞子鋼為朔方節度使杜希全賓佐，希全以鋼攝豐州刺史。

translations.literal: Xi's son Gang served on the staff of Shuofang Military Governor Du Xiquan; Xiquan had Gang act as Prefect of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Gang was on the staff of Shuofang Military Governor Du Xiquan, who put him in charge as acting Prefect of Feng.

sentences.zh: 晞以鋼幼弱，恐不任邊職，貞元七年，晞上章請罷鋼官。

translations.literal: Xi, because Gang was young and weak, feared he could not bear border duty; in the seventh year of Zhenyuan Xi submitted a memorial asking that Gang be removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was still young and frail, and Xi feared he was unfit for frontier command. In Zhenyuan 7 (791) Xi memorialized to have him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 德宗遣中使召之，鋼疑以他事見攝，乃單騎走入吐蕃。

translations.literal: Dezong sent a palace envoy to summon him; Gang suspected he was being summoned on other grounds, and alone on horseback fled into Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong sent a palace envoy to summon him. Gang feared he was being called up for some other reason and fled alone on horseback into Tibetan territory.

sentences.zh: 蕃將見鋼獨叛，不納，置之筏上，流入黃河令歸，杜希全得之，送赴京師，賜鋼自盡，晞亦坐子免官。

translations.literal: A Tibetan general, seeing Gang had defected alone, would not receive him; he was placed on a raft, set adrift into the Yellow River and sent back; Du Xiquan seized him and sent him to the capital; Gang was ordered to commit suicide; Xi was also removed from office because of his son.
translations.idiomatic: A Tibetan officer, seeing that Gang had come over alone, refused to take him in. They put him on a raft and set him adrift on the Yellow River to send him home. Du Xiquan captured him and forwarded him to the capital, where Gang was ordered to kill himself. Xi lost his post as punishment for his son.

sentences.zh: 明年，復授太子賓客。

translations.literal: The next year he was again appointed Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was again made Companion of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年卒，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan, he died; posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan, he died and was posthumously made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 晞次子鈞。

translations.literal: Xi's second son Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's second son was Jun.

sentences.zh: 鈞子承嘏別有傳。

translations.literal: Jun's son Chenggu has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son Chenggu is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 子 曖曖，子儀第六子。

translations.literal: Son Nuan. Nuan was Ziyi's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nuan. Nuan was Ziyi's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，尚代宗第四女升平公主，時升平年亦與暖相類。

translations.literal: When he was just over ten years old he married Daizong's fourth daughter, Princess Shengping; at the time Shengping's age was also much like Nuan's.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his early teens he married Daizong's fourth daughter, Princess Shengping, who was about the same age.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，恩寵冠於戚里，歲時錫賚珍玩，不可勝紀，

translations.literal: In the Dali era his favor surpassed all consort kin; yearly gifts of precious curios were beyond counting,
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign his favor outshone every other connection of the imperial consort clans; the court's yearly gifts of rare treasures could not be numbered,

sentences.zh: 大歷十三年，有詔毀除白渠水支流碾硙，以妨民溉田。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dali, there was an edict to destroy the tributary water mills of the White Canal, because they obstructed the people's irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Dali, an edict went out to tear down the White Canal's branch-line water mills, which were blocking farmers' irrigation.

sentences.zh: 升平有脂粉硙兩輪，郭子儀私硙兩輪，所司未敢毀徹。

translations.literal: Shengping had two cosmetic-powder mills; Guo Ziyi privately had two mills; the responsible office did not dare destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: The princess kept two mills for grinding face powder; Guo Ziyi privately owned two as well—and the officials did not dare touch them.

sentences.zh: 公主見代宗訴之，帝謂公主曰：「吾行此詔，蓋為蒼生，爾豈不識我意耶？

translations.literal: The princess saw Daizong and complained; the emperor said to the princess: "I am carrying out this edict for the sake of the common people—do you not understand my intent?
translations.idiomatic: The princess went to Daizong to protest. The emperor told her, "I issue this edict for the people's sake. Do you not grasp my meaning?

sentences.zh: 可為眾率先。」

translations.literal: You can take the lead for the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: You ought to set the example for everyone else."

sentences.zh: 公主即日命毀。

translations.literal: The princess that very day ordered them destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the princess ordered her mills torn down.

sentences.zh: 由是勢門碾硙八十餘所，皆毀之。

translations.literal: Thereupon more than eighty mills belonging to powerful families were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: After that, more than eighty mills owned by the great clans were demolished.

sentences.zh: 曖檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Nuan was made Acting Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Nuan was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 建中末，公主坐事，留之禁中，曖亦不令出入。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianzhong era the princess was implicated in an affair and detained in the palace; Nuan too was not allowed to come or go.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Jianzhong the princess was caught up in a scandal and kept within the palace precincts; Nuan was likewise forbidden to leave.

sentences.zh: 既而朱泚之亂，不知車駕幸奉天，為賊所逼，欲授偽官，曖辭以居喪被疾。

translations.literal: Then came Zhu Ci's rebellion; not knowing the imperial carriage had gone to Fengtian, they were pressed by the rebels who wished to grant them false offices; Nuan declined on the grounds of mourning and illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled they did not yet know the emperor had fled to Fengtian. The rebels closed in and tried to confer bogus posts on them; Nuan pleaded mourning and sickness.

sentences.zh: 既而與兄晞、弟曙及升平公主皆奔奉天，德宗喜，並釋前咎，待之如初，復銀青光祿大夫、檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he fled with his elder brother Xi, younger brother Shu, and Princess Shengping to Fengtian; Dezong was pleased; all previous faults were forgiven; they were treated as before; he was restored to Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he escaped with his brother Xi, his brother Shu, and Princess Shengping to join the emperor at Fengtian. Dezong was overjoyed, pardoned their earlier troubles, and received them as of old. Nuan was restored to Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從駕至山南，改太常卿同正員。

translations.literal: Following the emperor to the lands south of the mountains, he was changed to Vice Minister of Ceremonies with full stipend.
translations.idiomatic: When the court withdrew south of the Qinling ranges he was made Vice Minister of Ceremonies with full salary.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，帝為皇孫廣陵郡王納曖女為妃。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era the emperor took a consort for his grandson, the Prince of Guangling, from Nuan's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan the emperor matched Nuan's daughter to his grandson, the Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 曖，貞元十六年七月卒，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Ai died in the seventh month of Zhenyuan year sixteen and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ai died in the seventh month of Zhenyuan year sixteen and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 升平公主，元和五年十月薨，贈虢國大長公主，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: Princess Shengping died in the tenth month of Yuanhe year five and was posthumously ennobled Grand Princess of Guo, with the posthumous name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Shengping died in the tenth month of Yuanhe year five and was posthumously ennobled Grand Princess of Guo, with the posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王即位，為憲宗皇帝，妃生穆宗皇帝，

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangling ascended the throne as Emperor Xianzong; his consort bore Emperor Muzong,
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangling later ascended as Emperor Xianzong; his consort became the mother of Emperor Muzong,

sentences.zh: 元和十五年，穆宗即位，尊郭妃為皇太后，詔曰：「追遠飾終，先王令典。況積仁累義，事已顯於身前；祥會慶傳，福遂流於天下。式光盛德，爰舉徽章，尊尊親親，於是乎在。皇太后父贈尚書左僕射曖，克荷崇構，有勞王家，孝友本於生知，英華發於事任，實修一德，歷仕三朝。建中末年，屬有大難，畢力扈駕，忘軀即戎，忠貞之節，國史明備。才高望洽，是膺沁水之祥；德厚流光，乃啟塗山之祚。肆予小子，獲纘大業，未展定申之命，敢緣褒紀之恩，俾繼維師，用不縟禮。可贈太傅。」曖子釗、鏦、銛。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanhe, Muzong came to the throne and honored Consort Guo as Empress Dowager. An edict said, "Pursuing the distant and adorning the end is a fine canon of the former kings. How much more when accumulated humaneness and amassed righteousness had already been manifest in his lifetime, and auspicious convergence and transmitted blessing have then flowed through the realm. To shine forth flourishing virtue, we now raise a splendid title; honoring the honored and loving the kin lie in this. Ai, the Empress Dowager's father, posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was able to shoulder the lofty structure and had labor for the royal house. Filial piety and fraternal kindness were rooted in what he knew from birth; heroic brilliance emerged in the offices he held. He truly cultivated unified virtue and served through three reigns. At the end of Jianzhong, when there was great disaster, he spent all his strength escorting the imperial carriage, forgot his own body and went to war; his loyal and steadfast integrity is clearly recorded in the national history. With high talent and a reputation that satisfied all, he deserved the auspiciousness of Qinshui; with deep virtue and flowing radiance, he opened the blessing of Tushan. Therefore I, the young one, having inherited the great enterprise, before setting forth a settled and repeated command, dare to follow the grace of praise and record, have him continue as sustaining teacher, and use no excessive ritual. He may be posthumously appointed Grand Mentor." Ai's sons were Zhao, Cong, and Xian.

He may be posthumously appointed Grand Mentor." Ai's sons were Zhao, Cong, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 曙，代宗朝累歷司農卿，居父憂。

translations.literal: Shu, in the Daizong era, successively held the post of Minister of Revenue and was in mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had served repeatedly as Minister of Revenue under Daizong and was observing mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 建中三年冬，舒王誼為淮西、山南諸大元帥，以曙檢校左庶子，為元帥府都押牙。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Jianzhong, Prince Shu Yi was made grand commander of Huai-Xi and the Shannan circuits; Shu was made Acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent and chief military adjutant of the command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Jianzhong 3 (782), Prince Shu Yi was made grand commander of Huai-Xi and Shannan; Shu became Acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent and chief adjutant of the command.

sentences.zh: 京城亂，從幸山南，轉太府卿。

translations.literal: When the capital fell into chaos he followed the emperor to the lands south of the mountains and was transferred to Minister of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital erupted in chaos he followed the emperor south of the mountains and was transferred to Minister of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 隨駕還京，拜左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Following the emperor back to the capital, he was appointed General of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the return to the capital he was made General of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞元末卒。

translations.literal: He died at the end of the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: He died near the close of the Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 曖子 釗釗，偉姿儀，身長七尺，方口豐下，沈默寡言。

translations.literal: Nuan's son Zhao—imposing in bearing, seven feet tall, square mouth and full jaw, silent and sparing of words.
translations.idiomatic: Nuan's son Zhao was a striking figure: seven feet tall, square-jawed and full-faced, quiet and sparing with speech.

sentences.zh: 母升平長公主。

translations.literal: His mother was the Princess Shengping.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Princess Shengping.

sentences.zh: 代宗朝，釗為外孫，恩寵逾等，起家為太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: In the Daizong era, as the emperor's grandson by marriage, his favor exceeded his rank; he began his career as Ceremonial Aide in the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daizong, as the emperor's grandson-in-law, he enjoyed favor beyond his station and entered service as Ceremonial Aide in the Ministry of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 德宗朝，累官至太子右庶子。

translations.literal: In the Dezong era he rose through successive posts to Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong he rose step by step to Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 元和初，為左金吾衛大將軍，充左街使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was General of the Left Golden Guard and Commissioner of the Left Street.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yuanhe he was General of the Left Golden Guard and Commissioner of the Left Street.

sentences.zh: 九年十一月，檢校工部尚書，兼邠州刺史，充邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year he was made Acting Minister of Works, concurrent Prefect of Bin, and Military Governor of Bin-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Yuanhe 9 (814) he was made Acting Minister of Works, Prefect of Bin, and Military Governor of Bin-Ning.

sentences.zh: 數歲，檢校戶部尚書，入為司農卿。

translations.literal: Several years later he was made Acting Minister of Revenue and entered the capital as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he was made Acting Minister of Revenue and recalled to the capital as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 釗，大勛之後，姻聯戚里，而謙和接物，恭慎自持，居家臨民，無驕怠之色，無奢侈之失，士君子重之。

translations.literal: Zhao, a descendant of great merit with marriage ties to the consort kin, yet humble in receiving others and reverent in self-restraint—at home and in governing the people he showed neither arrogance nor extravagance; gentlemen esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was heir to towering merit and bound by marriage to the imperial kin, yet he met others with humility and held himself with sober care. In private life and in office he showed neither pride nor excess, and men of worth respected him.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，憲宗寢疾彌旬，諸中貴人秉權者欲議廢立，紛紛未定。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year Emperor Xianzong lay bedridden for more than ten days; powerful eunuchs who held sway wished to debate deposing and enthroning, and opinions were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yuanhe 15 (820) Xianzong lay gravely ill for more than ten days. The eunuchs in power began to murmur about deposing one emperor and raising another, and the court could not settle the question.

sentences.zh: 穆宗在東宮，心甚憂之，遣人問計於釗，釗曰：「殿下身為皇太子，但旦夕視膳，謹守以俟，又何慮乎！」

translations.literal: Muzong, as crown prince, was deeply worried; he sent someone to ask Zhao's counsel; Zhao said: "Your Highness is the crown prince—simply attend morning and evening at the imperial meals, guard your place and wait—what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: Muzong, still crown prince, was deeply anxious and sent to ask Zhao's advice. Zhao said, "You are the heir—attend the emperor morning and evening at table, keep your post, and wait. What cause for worry is there?"

sentences.zh: 迄今稱釗得元舅之體。

translations.literal: To this day Zhao is praised as having attained the deportment of a true primary maternal kinsman of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Even now Zhao is remembered as the very model of how an imperial uncle-by-marriage ought to comport himself.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，冊皇太后南內，推崇外氏，以釗兼司農卿。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne he enfeoffed the Empress Dowager in the Southern Inner Palace and elevated his maternal kin; Zhao was concurrently made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne he installed the Empress Dowager in the Southern Inner Palace and raised up the maternal clan; Zhao was given concurrent appointment as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校戶部尚書，充河陽三城懷節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Acting Minister of Revenue and Military Governor of the He-Yang Three Cities and Huai Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made Acting Minister of Revenue and Military Governor of He-Yang Three Cities and Huai.

sentences.zh: 歲中，換河中尹、河中晉絳慈隰節度使。

translations.literal: Within the year he was transferred to Intendant of Hezhong and Military Governor of Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he was shifted to Intendant of Hezhong and Military Governor of Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Sui.

sentences.zh: 釗歷踐籓鎮，以汾陽胄胤，材能選用，不獨憑椒房之勢，所蒞簡約不撓，其俗自理。

translations.literal: Zhao served in succession across the provinces; as heir of Fenyang he was chosen for ability, not relying solely on consort connections; what he governed was plain and unyielding, and local custom righted itself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao held one frontier post after another. As a scion of Fenyang he was appointed for talent, not merely for palace ties. His rule was spare and firm, and wherever he went order took hold of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位，尊郭太后為太皇太后，征釗為兵部尚書，兼檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When Jingzong ascended the throne he honored Empress Dowager Guo as Grand Empress Dowager and summoned Zhao as Minister of War, concurrently Acting Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong took the throne he raised Empress Dowager Guo to Grand Empress Dowager and recalled Zhao as Minister of War with concurrent Acting Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Prefect of Zizhou and Military Governor of Eastern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent out as Prefect of Zizhou and Military Governor of Eastern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，加司空。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne he was given the honorific Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong took the throne Zhao was given the honorific Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 大和三年冬，南蠻陷巂州，遂寇西川，杜元穎失於控禦，蠻軍陷成都府外城。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dahe, in winter the southern barbarians took Qiong Prefecture and then raided western Sichuan; Du Yuanying failed in control; the barbarian army took the outer wall of Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dahe, that winter the southern tribes seized Qiong Prefecture and swept into western Sichuan. Du Yuanying lost control, and the barbarians broke through the outer wall of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 朝廷未暇除帥，乃以釗兼領西川節度。

translations.literal: The court had no leisure to appoint a commander and so had Zhao concurrently take command of western Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The court had no time to find a new commander and put Zhao in charge of western Sichuan as well.

sentences.zh: 蠻軍已寇樟州，諸道援軍未至，川軍寡弱，不可令戰。

translations.literal: The barbarian army had already raided Zhang Prefecture; relief armies from the various circuits had not arrived; the Sichuan army was few and weak and could not be sent to battle.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had already struck Zhang Prefecture. Reinforcements from the circuits had not come, and the Sichuan forces were too few and weak to fight.

sentences.zh: 釗致書於蠻首領泬巔，責以侵寇之意，泬巔曰：「杜元穎不守疆埸，屢侵吾圉，以是修報也。」

translations.literal: Zhao sent a letter to the barbarian chieftain Juedian, reproaching him for the meaning of the invasion; Juedian said: "Du Yuanying does not guard the border and has repeatedly encroached on our territory—therefore we repay the injury."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao wrote to the barbarian leader Juedian, demanding why he had invaded. Juedian replied, "Du Yuanying neglects the frontier and keeps trespassing on our lands—that is why we have come to settle the score."

sentences.zh: 與釗修好而退。

translations.literal: He made peace with Zhao and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He then made peace with Zhao and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，授成都尹、劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: The court praised this; he was appointed Intendant of Chengdu and Military Governor of Western Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him and appointed him Intendant of Chengdu and Military Governor of Western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 與南詔立約，疆陲不擾。

translations.literal: He made a treaty with Nanzhao; the border was not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He concluded a pact with Nanzhao, and the frontier knew peace.

sentences.zh: 以疾求代。

translations.literal: Because of illness he asked to be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Illness drove him to ask for a successor.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為太常卿、檢校司徒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered the capital as Minister of Ceremonies and Acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to the capital as Minister of Ceremonies and Acting Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 十二月，在道卒，詔贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died on the road; an edict posthumously made him Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he died on the journey home; the throne posthumously made him Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 子仲文、仲辭。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhongwen and Zhongci.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhongwen and Zhongci.

sentences.zh: 曖子 鏦鏦，母升平長公主，大歷、貞元之間，恩禮冠諸主。

translations.literal: Nuan's son Cong—his mother was the Princess Shengping; between the Dali and Zhenyuan eras his honors and courtesy surpassed all princess consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Nuan's son Cong, born of Princess Shengping, enjoyed honors and deference unmatched among imperial sons-in-law between the Dali and Zhenyuan reigns.

sentences.zh: 順宗在東宮，以女德陽郡主尚鏦，時鏦與公主年未及冠，郡主尤為德宗之所鐘愛，故鏦之貴寵，焜燿一時。

translations.literal: When Shunzong was crown prince he gave his daughter, the Princess of Deyang Commandery, in marriage to Cong; at the time Cong and the princess had not yet reached the capping age; the princess was especially beloved by Dezong, and so Cong's noble favor blazed for a time.
translations.idiomatic: While Shunzong was heir apparent he married his daughter, Princess Deyang, to Cong. Both were still under age, and because the princess was a particular favorite of Dezong, Cong's glory at court burned brighter than anyone's for a season.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，改封德陽為漢陽公主。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended the throne Deyang was re-enfeoffed as Princess of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong took the throne, Deyang was re-enfeoffed as Princess of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 鏦累官至衛尉卿、駙馬都尉，改殿中監。

translations.literal: Cong rose through successive posts to Minister of the Palace Studs and Commandant-Consort, then was changed to Director of the Palace Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Cong rose to Minister of the Palace Studs and Commandant-Consort, then was reassigned as Director of the Palace Administration.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，鏦為叔舅，改右金吾衛大將軍、兼御史大夫，充左街使。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne Cong, as maternal uncle to the emperor, was changed to General of the Right Golden Guard, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Commissioner of the Left Street.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, Cong—as the emperor's uncle by marriage—was made General of the Right Golden Guard, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Commissioner of the Left Street.

sentences.zh: 城南有汾陽王別墅，林泉之致，莫之與比，穆宗常遊幸之，置酒極歡而罷，賜鏦甚厚。

translations.literal: South of the city was the Prince of Fenyang's villa; its forest streams had a charm none could match; Muzong often visited for pleasure; feasts were set out to the utmost joy before dispersing; Cong was rewarded very lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: South of the city stood the Prince of Fenyang's country estate, whose woods and waters had no rival. Muzong often went there to revel; wine was poured until mirth ran highest, and Cong was rewarded with extraordinary generosity.

sentences.zh: 俄加檢校工部尚書，兼太子詹事，充閑廄宮苑使。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Acting Minister of Works, concurrent Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Commissioner of the Imperial Stud and Palace Parks.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was further made Acting Minister of Works, Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Commissioner of the Imperial Stud and Palace Parks.

sentences.zh: 從容貴位三十餘年，而椒房之寵，國舅之恩，近代已來，無有其比。

translations.literal: At ease in noble rank for more than thirty years, yet in consort favor and imperial-uncle grace, in recent times none had his equal.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty years he moved at ease among the highest ranks, and in palace favor and privilege as imperial uncle, none in living memory had stood so high.

sentences.zh: 而鏦恭遜虔恪，不以富貴驕人，士無賢不肖，接之以禮，由是中外稱之。

translations.literal: Yet Cong was reverent, modest, and devout, not arrogant despite wealth and rank; toward gentlemen, worthy or not, he received them with courtesy; therefore he was praised within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cong remained reverent, modest, and sincere, never haughty in his riches. Scholar or scoundrel, he met all with courtesy, and won praise throughout the court and beyond.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年十月卒，贈尚書左僕射，仍以其弟銛代鏦為太子詹事，充閑廄宮苑使。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth month of Changqing year two and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. His younger brother Xian was appointed to succeed Cong as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent and Commissioner of the Imperial Stud and Palace Parks.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of Changqing year two and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. His younger brother Xian was appointed to succeed Cong as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent and Commissioner of the Imperial Stud and Palace Parks.

sentences.zh: 仲文，大和末為殿中少監。

translations.literal: Zhongwen served at the end of the Taihe era as Assistant Director of the Palace Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen served at the end of the Taihe era as Assistant Director of the Palace Administration.

sentences.zh: 開成初，詔仲文襲父太原郡公，制上，給事中封敕奏曰：「伏準制書，贈司徒郭釗嫡男仲文襲封太原郡公者，臣近訪知郭釗妻沈氏，公主之女，代宗皇帝外孫，有男仲辭，已選尚主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng an edict had Zhongwen inherit his father's title Duke of Taiyuan Commandery; when the decree was read out, Supervising Secretary Feng Jiao memorialized: "I respectfully note the decree: the posthumous Minister of Education Guo Zhao's legitimate son Zhongwen inherits the enfeoffment as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery. I have recently learned that Guo Zhao's wife, Lady Shen—a daughter of the princess and grandson-in-law of Emperor Daizong—has a son Zhongci, already chosen to marry a princess.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaicheng an edict named Zhongwen heir to his father's title, Duke of Taiyuan. When the decree was promulgated, Supervising Secretary Feng Jiao submitted: "The decree appoints Zhongwen, legitimate son of the late Minister of Education Guo Zhao, to inherit the Dukedom of Taiyuan. I have lately learned that Zhao's wife Lady Shen—daughter of a princess and granddaughter-in-law of Daizong—has a son Zhongci already selected to marry a princess.

sentences.zh: 仲文不合假冒，自稱嫡子。

translations.literal: Zhongwen ought not falsely claim the title and call himself the legitimate son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen has no right to pose as the legitimate heir.

sentences.zh: 若仲文承嫡，即沈氏須黜居別室，仲辭不合配尚貴主。

translations.literal: If Zhongwen inherits as legitimate heir, then Lady Shen must be demoted to a separate chamber, and Zhongci may not properly be matched to marry an honored princess.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhongwen takes the succession as legitimate son, Lady Shen must be relegated to a separate household, and Zhongci cannot remain fit to marry an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 伏以郭仲文，尚父子儀之孫，太皇太后之侄，戚里勛門，無與儔比，婚姻嫡庶，朝野具知，奪宗之配，實玷風教。

translations.literal: Consider that Guo Zhongwen is the grandson of Minister of State Ziyi and nephew of the Grand Empress Dowager—a consort clan and house of merit without peer; the question of legitimate versus secondary marriage is known throughout court and country; to wrest a princess's match would truly stain public morals.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhongwen is Ziyi's grandson and the Grand Empress Dowager's nephew—a union of merit and palace kin without parallel. Who in court or countryside does not know the facts of his birth? To overturn Zhongci's imperial match would be a scandal to the realm.

sentences.zh: 且仲文、仲辭既非同出，襲封尚主，不可並行。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhongwen and Zhongci were not born of the same mother; inheriting the enfeoffment and marrying a princess cannot both proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Zhongwen and Zhongci are not full brothers; one cannot both inherit the title and keep the princess marriage intact.

sentences.zh: 伏請付臺勘當。」

translations.literal: I respectfully request that the matter be referred to the Censorate for investigation."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the case be sent to the Censorate for inquiry."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「以萬年縣尉仲辭襲封。」仲文落下，以太皇太后侄，不之罪。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Let Zhongci, county commandant of Wannian, inherit the fief." Zhongwen was removed from consideration, but as the Grand Empress Dowager's nephew he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "Let Zhongci, county commandant of Wannian, inherit the fief." Zhongwen was removed from consideration, but as the Grand Empress Dowager's nephew he was not punished.

sentences.zh: 尋以仲辭為銀青光祿大夫、檢校中少監、駙馬都尉，襲封太原郡公，尚饒陽公主。

translations.literal: Soon Zhongci was made Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Assistant Director of the Palace Administration, Commandant-Consort, inheriting the title Duke of Taiyuan Commandery, and married to Princess Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhongci was made Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Assistant Director of the Palace Administration, and Commandant-Consort; he inherited the Dukedom of Taiyuan and married Princess Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 又仲辭兄詹事府丞仲恭，為銀青光祿大夫，尚金堂公主。

translations.literal: Also Zhongci's elder brother Zhonggong, a secretary in the Tutor of the Heir Apparent's office, was made Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and married to Princess Jintang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongci's elder brother Zhonggong, a clerk in the Heir Apparent's household, was likewise made Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and married Princess Jintang.

sentences.zh: 母弟 幼明幼明，尚父子儀之母弟也。

translations.literal: Younger maternal brother Youming—Youming was the younger brother of Ziyi's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Younger maternal brother Youming. Youming was the younger brother of Ziyi's mother.

sentences.zh: 性謹願無過，不工武藝，喜賓客飲宴，居家禦眾，皆得其歡心。

translations.literal: By nature cautious and guileless, without fault; not skilled in martial arts; he delighted in hosting guests and banquets; in managing the household and facing the multitude he won everyone's goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: He was cautious and plain, without reproach; no warrior, but fond of guests and feasts. At home and among neighbors he won every heart.

sentences.zh: 以子儀勛業，累歷大卿監，大歷八年卒，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: On the strength of Ziyi's achievements he rose through high ministerial offices. He died in Dali year eight and was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of Ziyi's achievements he rose through high ministerial offices. He died in Dali year eight and was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子昕，肅宗末為四鎮留後。

translations.literal: His son Xin, at the end of the Suzong era, was acting commander of the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin, in the closing years of Suzong, served as acting commander of the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 自關、隴陷蕃，為虜所隔，其四鎮、北庭使額，李嗣業、荔非元禮皆遙領之。

translations.literal: Since Guan and Long fell to Tibet he was cut off by the enemy; the commission posts of the Four Garrisons and Beiting—Li Siye and Lifei Yuanli both held them in name from afar.
translations.idiomatic: After Guan and Long were lost to Tibet he was sealed off behind enemy lines. The Four Garrisons and Beiting commissions were held only in name from afar—first by Li Siye, then by Lifei Yuanli.

sentences.zh: 昕阻隔十五年，建中二年，與伊西北庭節度使李元忠俱遣使於朝，德宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Xin was cut off for fifteen years. In the second year of Jianzhong, he and Li Yuanzhong, Military Governor of Yi-Xi and Beiting, both sent envoys to court, and Dezong praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was cut off for fifteen years. In the second year of Jianzhong, he and Li Yuanzhong, Military Governor of Yi-Xi and Beiting, both sent envoys to court, and Dezong praised them.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「四鎮、二庭，統任西夏五十七蕃十姓部落，國朝以來，相次率職。自關、隴失守，東西阻絕，忠義之徒，泣血相守，慎固封略，奉尊朝法，皆候伯守將交修共理之所致也。伊西北庭節度使李元忠，可北庭大都護；四鎮節度留後郭昕，可安西大都護、四鎮節度使。其將吏已下敘官，可超七資。」

translations.literal: The edict said, "The Four Garrisons and the Two Courts command and administer the fifty-seven barbarian groups and the ten-surname tribes of Western Xia. Since the beginning of the dynasty, they have successively fulfilled their duties. Since Guan and Long were lost and east and west were cut off from one another, loyal and righteous men have held guard with tears of blood, carefully securing the frontiers and reverently upholding the court's laws. This has all been brought about by regional lords, garrison commanders, and generals cultivating and governing together. Li Yuanzhong, Military Governor of Yi-Xi and Beiting, may be Protector-General of Beiting; Guo Xin, Acting Military Governor of the Four Garrisons, may be Protector-General of Anxi and Military Governor of the Four Garrisons. In assigning offices to their generals, officials, and those below them, they may be advanced seven grades beyond the norm."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "The Four Garrisons and the Two Courts command and administer the fifty-seven barbarian groups and the ten-surname tribes of Western Xia. Since the beginning of the dynasty, they have successively fulfilled their duties. Since Guan and Long were lost and east and west were cut off from one another, loyal and righteous men have held guard with tears of blood, carefully securing the frontiers and reverently upholding the court's laws. This has all been brought about by regional lords, garrison commanders, and generals cultivating and governing together. Li Yuanzhong, Military Governor of Yi-Xi and Beiting, may be Protector-General of Beiting; Guo Xin, Acting Military Governor of the Four Garrisons, may be Protector-General of Anxi and Military Governor of the Four Garrisons. In assigning offices to their generals, officials, and those below them, they may be advanced seven grades beyond the norm."

sentences.zh: 李元忠，本姓曹，名令忠，以功賜姓名。

translations.literal: Li Yuanzhong's original surname was Cao and his name Lingzhong; for merit he was granted the surname and name [Li Yuanzhong].
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanzhong had originally been surnamed Cao and named Lingzhong; for his service the throne bestowed the surname Li and the name Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時昕使自回紇歷諸蕃部，方達於朝。

translations.literal: At the time Xin's envoy, coming through the Uyghurs and passing through the various tribal lands, had just reached court.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's envoy had traveled through Uyghur territory and the western tribes and had only just arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 又有袁光庭者，為伊州刺史，隴右諸郡皆陷，光庭堅守伊州，吐蕃攻之累年，兵盡食竭，光庭先刃其妻子，自焚而死。

translations.literal: There was also Yuan Guangting, who was Prefect of Yizhou; all the Longyou commanderies fell, yet Guangting held Yizhou firm; Tibet attacked for years; troops were exhausted and food depleted; Guangting first killed his wife and children with a blade and then burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Yuan Guangting, Prefect of Yizhou. Every Longyou commandery fell, yet Guangting held Yizhou. The Tibetans besieged him for years until his soldiers were spent and his stores gone. He first cut down his wife and children, then set himself ablaze.

sentences.zh: 因昕使知之，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: Because of Xin's envoy this became known; [Guangting] was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the court through Xin's envoy, and Guangting was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：天寶之季，盜起幽陵，萬乘播遷，兩都覆沒。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: At the end of Tianbao, bandits rose at Youling; the ten-thousand-chariot ruler was driven to wander; the two capitals were overrun.
translations.idiomatic: The court historian writes: In the closing years of Tianbao rebellion broke out on the northern frontier; the emperor was driven into exile; both capitals fell.

sentences.zh: 天祚土德，實生汾陽。

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate is the virtue of earth; truly Fenyang was born of it.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's favor rests on the virtue of earth—and from that virtue Fenyang was born.

sentences.zh: 自河朔班師，關西殄寇，身扞豺虎，手披荊榛。

translations.literal: From withdrawing the army from Hebei to extinguishing bandits in Guanxi, he personally barred jackals and tigers and with his own hands cleared thorns and brambles.
translations.idiomatic: From the withdrawal from Hebei to the crushing of rebels in the west, he himself stood between the throne and the wolves, clearing the thorn path with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 七八年間，其勤至矣，再造王室，勛高一代。

translations.literal: For seven or eight years his toil reached its utmost; he restored the royal house; his merit towered over a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight years of labor brought the dynasty back from the brink; his achievement stood above his age.

sentences.zh: 及國威復振，群小肆讒，位重懇辭，失寵無怨。

translations.literal: When the state's prestige was restored, petty men unleashed slander; though his rank was weighty he earnestly declined, and though he lost favor he bore no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire regained its strength, small men whispered poison; though honors piled upon him he repeatedly begged off, and though the throne turned cool he nursed no grudge.

sentences.zh: 不幸危而邀君父，不挾憾以報仇讎，晏然效忠，有死無二，誠大雅君子，社稷純臣。

translations.literal: Though imperiled he did not hold the ruler and father hostage; though wronged he did not repay enemies with malice; calmly he rendered loyalty, with death he knew no second heart—truly a gentleman of the grand style, a pure minister of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In peril he never seized upon the emperor as leverage; wronged, he never repaid his foes in kind. He served in tranquil fidelity, ready to die without a second thought—a great-hearted gentleman and a true pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 自秦、漢已還，勛力之盛，無與倫比。

translations.literal: Since Qin and Han, in the splendor of merit and strength none can be compared with him.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin and Han, no servant of the throne has matched the scale of his service.

sentences.zh: 而晞、曖於缞粗之中，拔身虎口，赴難奉天，可謂忠孝之門有嗣矣。

translations.literal: Yet Xi and Nuan, still in coarse hemp mourning, pulled themselves from the tiger's maw and rushed to Fengtian in the crisis—one may say the house of loyalty and filial piety had heirs.
translations.idiomatic: And Xi and Nuan, still clad in mourning hemp, tore themselves from the tiger's jaws to reach Fengtian in the emperor's hour of need—the loyal and filial line had not gone barren.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：猗歟汾陽，功扶昊蒼。

translations.literal: In praise: How grand Fenyang, whose merit upholds the azure heavens!
translations.idiomatic: In praise: O Fenyang, grand in merit, upholding the wide sky!

sentences.zh: 秉仁蹈義，鐵心石腸。

translations.literal: Upholding benevolence and treading righteousness—iron heart and stone bowels.
translations.idiomatic: He held to benevolence and walked in righteousness—a heart of iron, a gut of stone.

sentences.zh: 四朝靜亂，五福其昌。

translations.literal: Through four reigns he stilled chaos; the five blessings flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Four reigns he quieted in turmoil; the five blessings bloomed in his house.

sentences.zh: 為臣之節，敢告忠良。

translations.literal: The measure of serving as minister—I dare report it to the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the standard of the minister—I lay it before the loyal and true.
